home.heading: Alexandra Fontner

intro.p1: Welcome to my page! Here you can get to know someone who loves expressing their human creativity through the means of digital technologies. I have interests in various fields, such as different types of software development (games, web, mobile) as well as art and animation in both 2D and 3D. Below you can view some of my projects and find more information about me and my skill set.
intro.p2: If you want to get in touch regarding work opportunities or have any questions about my projects, do not hesitate to reach out to me via email or LinkedIn:

projectsTexts.p1: Here I want to present some of the projects that I created or contributed to, to show what kind of work I am capable of and also enjoy doing. Hopefully more will be added over time as I continue learning.
projectsTexts.p2: To gain a more in-depth look on some of them, you are also welcome to take a look at my profiles on ArtStation or GitHub:

home.universityText: These are some of the projects that I made for university courses. There are more of course, but I tried to select a nice variety out of those that showcase my different skills and that I am the most proud of.
home.personalText: These are personal projects that I have been working on in my free time to improve my skills and/or learn new things. Due to university I do not always have a lot of time for them, but I hope they will continue to grow in the coming years. This website itself is one of them as well of course, designed from scratch in Figma and implemented using Angular and Tailwind.

biography.p1: I have always had a wide range of interests and enjoyed learning new things and expressing myself creatively. When I was a teenager and had to start thinking about what I wanted to do after school, I decided that I would like to work on computer games, either as an artist or developer. I have always enjoyed playing them (with some of my favourites nowadays being the two Kingdom Come: Deliverance games, Medieval Dynasty, and Stellaris, among many others), and the thought of contributing to the creation of future games was very exciting to me.
biography.p2: After school I applied for the bachelor programme Creative Computing, where got to know various other use cases for programming besides games, and discovered that for example web applications and mobile apps can be super fun to develop as well. By now I have about two years of professional experience as a frontend web developer, and I would be very happy to both deepen my knowledge in this area, as well as expand my skills into other fields.
biography.p3: While I agree that AI technologies can be an effective tool in software development if used as an assistive measure on top of one's own knowledge and skills, I also want to be open about the fact that I do not use generative AI tools for any of my creative work (writing, illustration, 3D art etc.). I simply enjoy the process of creating these myself much more, and it would be quite stupid of me to outsource precisely the fun work to AI, wouldn't you agree?
